statement.p: Line \ell_1 contains the points {\left(-5,9\right)} and {\left(-8,-6\right)}\text{.} Line \ell_2 contains the points {\left(9,0\right)} and {\left(10,5\right)}\text{.}

solution.p: The first lines slope is {5} and the second lines slope is also {5}\text{.} So either the two lines are the same line, or they are parallel.

In point-slope form, the first line has an equation y={5}(x + 5)+9\text{,} and the second line has an equation y={5}(x-9)+0\text{.} In slope-intercept form, these are y={5x+34} and y={5x-45}\text{.} So the two lines have different y-intercepts and must be distinct lines.
